which provides valuable variables and information on commuting for the
Canadian population aged 15 and older living in private households.

# Section objectives

In the previous section, we developed spatial filters to address the
likely endogeneity between accessibility measures and individual
outcomes. Building on this, we now develop regression models to examine
the relationship between job accessibility and employment outcomes. 

## Suggested Readings

-   Bastiaanssen, J., Johnson, D., & Lucas, K. (2025). *The relationship
    between individual employment probabilities and accessibility to
    matching jobs: A study of the Netherlands*. Transportation Research
    Part A: Policy and Practice, 193, 104398.
-   Cunningham, S. (2021). *Causal inference: The mixtape*. Yale
    university press.

# Models

There are many ways in which we can model the relationship between accessibility and employment outcomes using statistical models, or more specifically, using regression models. For instance, in terms of the type of outcome (categorical, ordinal-categorical,
binomial, linear), the type of accessibility measure (e.g., gravity,
spatial availability), and the population sample.

Here, we will demonstrate the following situations:

+-------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+
| Population  | Measure     | Outcome\    | Regression  |
|             |             | (Variable - | Model       |
|             |             | Type)       |             |

| force       | Spatial     | income of   | Linear      |
|             | A           | census      | Regression  |
|             | vailability | family\     |             |
|             | (SA)        | (           |             |
|             |             | *CFINC_AT*: |             |
|             |             | Linear)     |             |
+-------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+
| Labour      | Multimodal  | Employment  | Weighted    |
| force       | Spatial     | status\     | Logistic    |
|             | A           | (           | Regression  |
|             | vailability | *LBR_FORC*: |             |
|             | (SA)        | Binomial)   |             |
+-------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+
| Unemployed  | Matching    | Job         | Weighted    |
| people      | Multimodal  | seeking\    | Multinomial |
| without an  | Spatial     | (LOKWK:     | Regression  |
| education   | A           | C           |             |
| certificate | vailability | ategorical) |             |
| or with a   | (MMSA)      |             |             |
| high school |             |             |             |
| degree as   |             |             |             |
| their       |             |             |             |
| maximum     |             |             |             |
| education   |             |             |             |
| level       |             |             |             |
+-------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+
| Unemployed  | Matching    | After-tax   | Weighted    |
| people      | Multimodal  | famile      | Ordinal     |
| without an  | Spatial     | income \    | Regression  |
| education   | A           | (           |             |
| certificate | vailability | *CFINC_AT:* |             |
| or with a   | (MMSA)      | Transformed |             |
| high school |             | into        |             |
| degree as   |             | quintiles)  |             |
| their       |             |             |             |
| maximum     |             |             |             |
| education   |             |             |             |
| level       |             |             |             |
+-------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+

: Regression models to be estimated.

For all models, we will consider the population weights. Therefore, we
will perform weighted regression models. In addition, for all cases, the
population used is the labour force or a subset of the labour force.

We start our regressions by modelling the effect of Multimodal Spatial
Availability (SA), without considering skill-job matching, on after-tax
family income. Considering that this outcome is continuous and has a
ratio scale (zero means an absence of money), we will perform a linear
regression. Next, using the same population sample and accessibility
measures, we will estimate a logistic regression to estimate the effect
of accessibility on the probability of being employed (outcome with a
binomial distribution).

Then, using a subset of the labour force, more specifically, unemployed
people without an education certificate or with a high school degree as
their maximum education level, we will estimate the effect of
accessibility on whether they are looking for a job or not (categorical,
since the outcome has three possible values: not looking for a job,
looking for a part-time job, or looking for a full-time job) using
multinomial logistic regression. Then, we will estimate the effect of
accessibility on the probability of being in an after-tax income
quintile using ordinal regression. For these two last models, we will
see the effect of Matching Multimodal Spatial Availability (MMSA), which
considers the skill-job matching.

Except for the multinomial regression, for which we will use the
[svyGAM](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/svyVGAM/index.html),
all other models will be estimated using
[survey](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/survey/index.html).

We will evaluate these variables as covariates:

-   Respondent's age (`AGE`)
-   Number of children under age 5 in the household (`CFKID0T5`)
-   Gender (`Gender`)
-   Disability indicator (`Disability`)
-   Residency status (`Temporary_or_refugee`)
-   Racialized identity (`Visible_minority`)
-   Number of weeks worked in the previous year (`Weeks`)
-   Single-parent household (`Single_parent`)
-   Family size (`CFCNT_PP`)
-   Population centre category (`Pop_centre`)
-   Population density (`Pop_density`)

In addition, we include the instrumental variables generated using the
spatial filters.

To address potential endogeneity, we apply a two-stage approach. For endogenous linear variables, we use the conventional Two-Stage Least Squares (2SLS) approach, while for endogenous variables in nonlinear models, we use the Two-Stage Residual Inclusion (2SRI) method. For both cases we have two steps:

- First stage: Regress each endogenous variable on its instrumental variable(s) and all exogenous covariates. For continuous endogenous variables, the predicted values are used in the second-stage model under conventional 2SLS. For the 2SRI models, the residuals from the first-stage regressions are used.
- Second stage: For models estimated using conventional 2SLS, replace the endogenous linear variables with their first-stage fitted (predicted) values. For the 2SRI models, include the first-stage residuals as additional regressors to account for potential endogeneity.

Setting the folder with the accessibility measures and spatial filter:

```{r}
study_area_label <- "PCD3520"
spatial_unit <- "CT"
spatial_unit_identifier <- "CTUID"

study_area_folder <- paste0(here::here(),"/data-raw/output/",
study_area_label,"/")
study_area_folder
```

We will assess two accessibility indicators:

-   Multimodal spatial availability (SA), considering active, public
    transit and car-motorized modes.
-   Matching multimodal spatial availability (MMSA), considering active,
    public transit and car-motorized mode, and education levels.

We selected measures with an active mode, instead of walking and
cycling, to reduce potential high-correlation between indicators.

```{r read-accessibility}
# Folder  
measures_folder <- paste0(study_area_folder,"/",spatial_unit,
                          "/spatial-filter-measures/")

# Read file
SA_mode <- read.csv(paste0(measures_folder, 
                           "SA_mode_active_sf.csv"), 
                    colClasses = c("character", "character",
                                   "numeric","numeric",
                                   "numeric","numeric")) %>% 
  mutate(PwMode_label = 
           case_when(PwMode_label == "Car-motorized" ~ "Car",
                     PwMode_label == "Public transit" ~ "Transit",
                     TRUE ~ PwMode_label)
         )
```

Converting the SA table to a wide table in order to link it with each
survey respondent:

```{r}
SA_mode_wide <- SA_mode %>%
  rename(SA = SA_im, 
         Sf_SA = Sf_SA_im,
         SA_pp = SA_pp_im,
         Sf_SA_pp = Sf_SA_pp_im
         ) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = spatial_unit_identifier,
              names_from = PwMode_label, 
              values_from = c(SA, SA_pp, Sf_SA, Sf_SA_pp),
              names_sep = "_") 

head(SA_mode_wide)
```

```{r read-MSSA}
# Read file
MMSA_mode <- read.csv(paste0(measures_folder, 
                             "MMSA_mode_education_active_sf.csv"), 
                    colClasses = c("character", "character","character",
                                   "numeric","numeric",
                                   "numeric","numeric")) %>% 
  mutate(PwMode_label = 
           case_when(PwMode_label == "Car-motorized" ~ "Car",
                     PwMode_label == "Public transit" ~ "Transit",
                     TRUE ~ PwMode_label)
         )
```

Converting the MMSA table to a wide table in order to link it with each
survey respondent:

```{r}
MMSA_mode_wide <- MMSA_mode %>%
  rename(MMSA = SA_ime, 
         Sf_MMSA = Sf_SA_ime,
         MMSA_pp = SA_pp_ime,
         Sf_MMSA_pp = Sf_SA_pp_ime
         ) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(spatial_unit_identifier, Education),
              names_from = PwMode_label, 
              values_from = c(MMSA, MMSA_pp, Sf_MMSA, Sf_MMSA_pp),
              names_sep = "_") 

head(MMSA_mode_wide)
```

## Preprocessing files

We will filter the census data frame by administrative (province and/or
census division) and/or statistical (census metropolitan areas and
census agglomerations)[^3]. The chunk below shows how to make this
procedure:

[^3]: As said before, we will perform our analysis for the city of
    Toronto. If you want to select a specific area to work, uncomment
    the code above that applies to your case and select the apropriate
    code of your interest unit. Please, check the dictionary to have
    more informations about the [provinces
    code](https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2021/ref/dict/tab/index-eng.cfm?ID=t1_8),
    [census
    divisions](https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2021/ref/dict/az/Definition-eng.cfm?ID=geo008),
    and [census metropolitan
    areas](https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2021/ref/dict/az/Definition-eng.cfm?ID=geo009)

```{r filter-boundaries}
pcd_codes <- "3520"

# Filtering by census division
 census_filtered <- census %>%
   # Only select respondents who live in  Toronto
                    filter(PCD %in% pcd_codes)
```

According to the census code book, the variable 'PwMode' has the
following possible values:

-   -3: Not applicable.
-   1: Car, truck or van - as a driver.
-   2: Car, truck or van - as a passenger.
-   3: Bus.
-   4: Subway or elevated rail.
-   5: Light rail, streetcar or commuter train.
-   6: Passenger ferry.
-   7: Walked.
-   8: Bicycle.
-   9: Motorcycle, scooter or moped.
-   10: Other method.

We'll rename the travel modes to facilitate the readability of the data.
Additionally, we'll remove from our analysis travel modes signed as
'Other methods':

According to the Census 2021, an 'Employed' person refers to those who,
during the reference period, had a labour force status of
'employed.'[^4]. In addition, the labour force is made up of the
employed population and the unemployed population. This variable can
assume the values:

[^4]: Those who, during the reference period: (a) Did any work at all at
    a job or business, that is, paid work in the context of an
    employer-employee relationship, or self-employment. This also
    includes persons who did unpaid family work, which is defined as
    unpaid work contributing directly to the operation of a farm,
    business or professional practice owned and operated by a related
    member of the same household; or (b) Had a job but were not at work
    due to factors such as their own illness or disability, personal or
    family responsibilities, vacation or a labour dispute. This category
    excludes persons not at work because they were on layoff or between
    casual jobs, and those who did not then have a job (even if they had
    a job to start at a future date).

-   -3: Not Applicable, \< 15 years
-   1: In Labour Force, Employed
-   2: In Labour Force, Unemployed
-   3: Not in Labour Force

```{r lf-selection}
census_vetting <- census_filtered  %>%
  dplyr::select("Frame_ID", "PRCDDA", "PR", "CMA",  "PCD",
                "POP_CNTR_IND","CompW1", "LBR_FORC", "CfInc_AT", 
                "CFCNT_PP", "CF_PnCF_NumEarners", "PWDA","PWPR", "PWCD", 
                "PWCMA", "PWDUR", "PWDist", "PwMode", "AGE",
                "HCDD_7V", "LayAB", "REASN", "MRNFY2", "PWStat", 
                "GENDER_BINARY", "LOLICOA", "LoLIMA", "ACTLMFLG", 
                "CFAMSTSIMPLE", "IMMCAT5", "PerImmA", "DVisMin", 
                "CFKID0T5", "Weeks", "LOKWK","Mob5", 
                "GovtI_SocAssist")

census_filtered <- census_filtered %>% 
  filter(LBR_FORC == 1 | LBR_FORC == 2) %>%
  dplyr::select(names(census_vetting))
```

According to the Census 2021, an 'Employed' person refers to those who,
during the reference period, had a labour force status of
'employed.'[^5]. In addition, the labour force is made up of the
employed population and the unemployed population. This variable can
assume the values:

[^5]: Those who, during the reference period: (a) Did any work at all at
    a job or business, that is, paid work in the context of an
    employer-employee relationship, or self-employment. This also
    includes persons who did unpaid family work, which is defined as
    unpaid work contributing directly to the operation of a farm,
    business or professional practice owned and operated by a related
    member of the same household; or (b) Had a job but were not at work
    due to factors such as their own illness or disability, personal or
    family responsibilities, vacation or a labour dispute. This category
    excludes persons not at work because they were on layoff or between
    casual jobs, and those who did not then have a job (even if they had
    a job to start at a future date).

-   -3: Not Applicable, \< 15 years (already previously excluded from
    our dataset)
-   1: In Labour Force, Employed
-   2: In Labour Force, Unemployed
-   3: Not in Labour Force (already previously excluded from our
    dataset)

According to the census code book, the variable 'GENDER_BINARY' has the
following possible values:[^6]

[^6]: Given that the non-binary population is small, data aggregation to
    a two-category gender variable is sometimes necessary to protect the
    confidentiality of responses provided. In these cases, individuals
    in the category "non-binary persons" are distributed into the other
    two gender categories and are denoted by the "+" symbol.

-   1: Woman+.
-   2: Man+.

According to the census code book, the variable 'GENDER_BINARY' has the
following possible values:

-   -3: Concept not applicable (collective households)
-   1: Not in low income
-   2: In low income
-   3: Concept not applicable (territories or reserves) - not in low
    income
-   4: Concept not applicable (territories or reserves) - in low income

According to the census code book, the variable 'LOLICOA' has the
following possible values:[\^]

[\^] Refers to the income situation of a person in relation to the
Low-income cut-offs, after-tax (LICO-AT). Persons with income that is
below this low-income line are considered to be in low income.

-   -3: Concept not applicable (collective households)
-   1: Not in low income
-   2: In low income
-   3: Concept not applicable (territories or reserves) - not in low
    income
-   4: Concept not applicable (territories or reserves) - in low income

According to the census code book, the variable 'LoLIMA' has the
following possible values:[\^]

[\^] Refers to the income situation of a person in relation to the
Low-income measure, after-tax (LIM-AT). Persons with income that is
below this low-income line are considered to be in low income.

-   -3: Concept not applicable (collective households)
-   1: Not in low income
-   2: In low income
-   3: Not in low income (territories or reserves)
-   4: In low income (territories or reserves)
-   5: Concept not applicable (collective households) - not in low
    income
-   6: Concept not applicable (collective households) - in low income

We will use the variable *ACTLMFLG - Activities of daily living: Flag*
as an indicative of disability, because the Census of Population does
not have a variable regarding disability. The question on activities of
daily living refers to difficulties a person may have doing certain
activities as a result of physical, cognitive, mental, or other
health-related conditions or problems. We will select all those
respondents who affirm to have frequent (always) difficulties to develop
regular activities. According to the census code book, the variable
'ACTLMFLG' has the following possible values:

-   -2: Not stated
-   1: Yes, always
-   2: Yes, often
-   3: Yes, sometimes
-   4: No

According to the census code book, the variable 'CFAMSTSIMPLE' has the
following possible values:

-   1: Married spouse or common-law partner
-   2: Parent in a one-parent family
-   3: Child
-   4: Person not in a census family

According to the census code book, the variable 'IMMCAT5' has the
following possible values:

-   1: Non-immigrants
-   2: Non-permanent residents3 Immigrants admitted before 1980
-   100010: Economic immigrants - Principal applicants
-   100020: Economic immigrants - Secondary applicants
-   200000: Immigrants sponsored by family
-   300000: Refugees
-   400000: Other immigrants

According to the census code book, "Visible minority" refers to whether
a person is a visible minority as defined by the Employment Equity Act.
The Employment Equity Act defines visible minorities as "persons, other
than Aboriginal peoples, who are non-Caucasian in race or non-white in
colour." The visible minority population consists mainly of the
following groups: South Asian, Chinese, Black, Filipino, Arab, Latin
American, Southeast Asian, West Asian, Korean and Japanese. The variable
'DVisMin' has the following possible values:

-   1: Other (not a visible minority)
-   2: South Asian
-   3: Chinese
-   4: Black
-   5: Filipino
-   6: Arab
-   7: Latin American
-   8: Southeast Asian
-   9: West Asian
-   10: Korean
-   11: Japanese
-   12: Visible minority, n.i.e.
-   13: Multiple visible minorities
-   14: Indigenous peoples

According to the census code book, the variable 'HCDD_7V'(Education:
Highest certificate, diploma or degree) has the following possible
values:

-   -3: Not applicable
-   1: No certificate, diploma or degree
-   2: High (secondary) school diploma or equivalency certificate
-   4: College, CEGEP or other non-university certificate or diploma
-   5: University certificate or diploma below bachelor level
-   6: Bachelor's degree or higher

In the next chunk, we will rename the travel modes to facilitate the
readability of the data.

```{r labelling-variables}
census_filtered_labeled <- census_filtered %>%
                   mutate(PwMode_label = 
                            case_when(PwMode > 0 & PwMode <= 2 ~ "Car",
                                      PwMode == 9 ~ "Car",
                                      PwMode >= 3 & PwMode <= 6  ~ "Transit",
                                      PwMode == 7  ~ "Active",
                                      PwMode == 8  ~ "Active", 
                                      PwMode == 10 ~ "Other",
                                      PwMode == -3 ~ "Not applicable"),
                          PwMode_label = factor(
                            PwMode_label, levels = c("Car", "Active","Transit",
                                                     "Not applicable","Other")),
                          # Walk 
                          Walk = 
                            case_when(PwMode == 7  ~ "Yes",
                                      TRUE ~ "No"),
                          Walk = factor(Walk, levels = c("No", "Yes")),
                     # Bike 
                          Bike = 
                            case_when(PwMode == 8 ~ "Yes",
                                      TRUE ~ "No"),
                          Bike = factor(Bike, levels = c("No", "Yes")),
                     # Active 
                          Transit = 
                            case_when(PwMode_label == "Transit"  ~ "Yes",
                                      TRUE ~ "No"),
                          Transit = factor(Transit, levels = c("No", "Yes")),
                     # Active 
                          Active = 
                            case_when(PwMode == 7  ~ "Yes",
                                      PwMode == 8  ~ "Yes", 
                                      TRUE ~ "No"),
                          Active = factor(Active, levels = c("No", "Yes")),
                     # Labour force
                     LBR_FORC_label = 
                            case_when(LBR_FORC == 1 ~ "Employed",
                                      LBR_FORC == 2 ~ "Unemployed"),
                          LBR_FORC_label = factor(LBR_FORC_label, 
                                                  levels = c("Unemployed",
                                                             "Employed")), 
                     # Gender 
                          Gender = 
                            case_when(GENDER_BINARY == 1 ~ "Woman+",
                                      GENDER_BINARY == 2 ~ "Man+"),
                          Gender = factor(Gender, levels = c("Man+", "Woman+")),
                     # Low income population - LOLICOA
                     LOLICOA_label = 
                       case_when(LOLICOA == -3 ~ "Not in low income", 
                                 LOLICOA == 1 ~ "Not in low income",
                                 LOLICOA == 2 ~ "In low income",
                                 LOLICOA == 3 ~ "Not in low income",
                                 LOLICOA == 4 ~ "In low income"),
                     LOLICOA_label = factor(LOLICOA_label), 
                    LoLIMA_label = 
                       case_when(LoLIMA == -3 ~ "Not in low income", 
                                 LoLIMA == 1 ~ "Not in low income",
                                 LoLIMA == 2 ~ "In low income",
                                 LoLIMA == 3 ~ "Not in low income",
                                 LoLIMA == 4 ~ "In low income",
                                 LoLIMA == 5 ~ "Not in low income",
                                 LoLIMA == 6 ~ "In low income"),
                     LoLIMA_label = factor(LoLIMA_label), 
                    Low_Income_label = 
                      case_when(
                        LoLIMA_label == "In low income" | 
                          LOLICOA_label == "In low income" ~ "In low income",
                                TRUE ~ "Not in low income"), 
                    Low_Income_label = factor(Low_Income_label, 
                                              levels = c("Not in low income", 
                                                         "In low income")), 
                    # Disability
                    Disability = 
                       case_when(ACTLMFLG == -2 ~ "No", 
                                 # Only always is set as disability
                                 ACTLMFLG == 1 ~ "Yes", 
                                 ACTLMFLG == 2 ~ "No",
                                 ACTLMFLG == 3 ~ "No",
                                 ACTLMFLG == 4 ~ "No"),
                    Disability = factor(Disability, levels = c("No", "Yes")), 
                    # Single-parent family
                    Single_parent = 
                       case_when(CFAMSTSIMPLE == 1 ~ "No",
                                 CFAMSTSIMPLE == 2 ~ "Yes",
                                 CFAMSTSIMPLE == 3 ~ "No",
                                 CFAMSTSIMPLE == 4 ~ "No"),
                    Single_parent = factor(Single_parent, 
                                           levels = c("No", "Yes")), 
                    # Citizenship
                    Temporary_or_refugee = 
                       case_when(IMMCAT5 == 2 ~ "Yes",
                         IMMCAT5 == 300000 ~ "Yes",
                                 TRUE ~ "No"),
                     Temporary_or_refugee = factor(Temporary_or_refugee, 
                                                   levels = c("No","Yes")), 
                    # New immigrant
                    PerImmA_label = 
                       case_when(PerImmA == 10 ~ "New immigrant",
                                 PerImmA != 10 ~ "Not a new immigrant"),
                     PerImmA_label = factor(PerImmA_label),
                    # Visible Minority (binary)
                    Visible_minority = 
                       case_when(DVisMin == 1 ~ "No",
                                 DVisMin != 1 ~ "Yes"),
                     Visible_minority = factor(Visible_minority, 
                                                   levels = c("No","Yes")), 
                    # Visible Minority (full-group)
                    DVisMin_label = 
                      case_when(DVisMin == 1  ~ "Other (not a visible minority)",
                                DVisMin == 2  ~ "South Asian",
                                DVisMin == 3  ~ "Chinese",
                                DVisMin == 4  ~ "Black",
                                DVisMin == 5  ~ "Filipino",
                                DVisMin == 6  ~ "Arab",
                                DVisMin == 7  ~ "Latin American",
                                DVisMin == 8  ~ "Southeast Asian",
                                DVisMin == 9  ~ "West Asian",
                                DVisMin == 10 ~ "Korean",
                                DVisMin == 11 ~ "Japanese",
                                DVisMin == 12 ~ "Visible minority, n.i.e.",
                                DVisMin == 13 ~ "Multiple visible minorities",
                                DVisMin == 14 ~ "Indigenous peoples"),
                    DVisMin_label = factor(DVisMin_label),
                    # AGE
                    AGE_label = 
                      case_when(AGE <= 24 ~ "Youth",
                                TRUE  ~ "Adult"),
                    AGE_label = factor(AGE_label), 
                    # Number of weeks worked in 2020 
                    Weeks = 
                      case_when(Weeks < 0 ~ 0, 
                                TRUE ~ Weeks), 
                    # Education
                    Education = case_when(
                      HCDD_7V %in% 1:2 ~ "High school or no certificate",
                      HCDD_7V %in% 3:4 ~ "College or apprenticeship certificate",
                      HCDD_7V %in% 5:6 ~ "University certificate or higher"),
                    Education = factor(
                      Education, 
                      levels = c("University certificate or higher", 
                                 "College or apprenticeship certificate",
                                 "High school or no certificate")),
                    # Looked for paid work in the previous month 
                    LOKWK_label = 
                      case_when(LOKWK == -5 ~ "Employed",
                                LOKWK == -3 ~ "Not applicable",
                                LOKWK == 1 ~  "No",
                                LOKWK == 2 ~  "Yes (for full-time work)",
                                LOKWK == 3 ~ "Yes (for part-time work)"),
                    LOKWK_label = factor(LOKWK_label, 
                                         levels = c("No", 
                                                    "Yes (for part-time work)",
                                                    "Yes (for full-time work)",
                                                     "Employed", 
                                                     "Not applicable")),
                    LOKWK_binary_label = case_when(LOKWK == -5 ~ "Employed",
                                LOKWK == -3 ~ "Not applicable",
                                LOKWK == 1 ~  "No",
                                LOKWK == 2 ~  "Yes",
                                LOKWK == 3 ~ "Yes"),
                    LOKWK_binary_label = factor(
                      LOKWK_binary_label, 
                      levels = c("No",
                                 "Yes", 
                                 "Employed", 
                                "Not applicable")),
                    # Population centre
                    Pop_centre =
                      case_when(POP_CNTR_IND == 1 ~ "Rural",
                                POP_CNTR_IND == 2 ~ "Small",
                                POP_CNTR_IND == 3 ~  "Medium",
                                POP_CNTR_IND == 4 ~  "Large"),
                    Pop_centre = factor(Pop_centre, levels = c("Large", 
                                                               "Medium",
                                                               "Small",
                                                               "Rural"))
                    
                    )
```

Creating neighborhood variables: unemployed rate, percentage of car
commuters, and DA population density.

```{r}
# Unemployment rate by DA
unemp_rate <- census_filtered_labeled %>%
  mutate(PRCDDA = as.character(PRCDDA)) %>%
  group_by(PRCDDA) %>%
  summarise(employed_w = sum(CompW1[LBR_FORC == 1], na.rm = TRUE),
    unemployed_w = sum(CompW1[LBR_FORC == 2], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(unemployment_rate = (unemployed_w/(employed_w+unemployed_w)) * 100)

# Car commuters rate 
car_rate <- census_filtered_labeled %>%
  mutate(PRCDDA = as.character(PRCDDA)) %>%
  group_by(PRCDDA) %>%
  summarise(car_w = sum(CompW1[PwMode_label == "Car"], na.rm = TRUE),
    total_w = sum(CompW1[!PwMode_label == "Not applicable"], na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(car_share = ifelse(total_w == 0, 0, (car_w/total_w) * 100))

# DA Population Density
pop_density_da <- dissemination_areas %>%
  mutate(DAUID = as.character(DAUID)) %>%
  mutate(Pop_density = DAPOPULATION / LANDAREA) %>% 
  dplyr::select(DAUID, Pop_density) %>% 
  st_drop_geometry()
```

Now, we create a table called respondents that will serve as the base
for building the regression models.


```{r}
respondents <- census_filtered_labeled %>% 
  mutate(PRCDDA = as.character(PRCDDA)) %>%
  left_join(access_vars, by = c("PRCDDA" = "DAUID",

                            ))%>%

            by = c("PRCDDA" = "DAUID")) %>%
  left_join(unemp_rate[,c("PRCDDA","unemployment_rate")],

            by = "PRCDDA")
```

To better approximate a causal relationship between accessibility and
employment outcomes, we restrict the sample according to the following
criteria:

-   We include only respondents who have lived at the same address for
    at least five years, in order to reduce residence self-selection
    bias.
-   We exclude individuals who did not work the full year due to illness
    or disability; pregnancy, maternity, or parental leave; full-time
    studies or training; caregiving responsibilities; or retirement.
    This restriction focuses the analysis on respondents for whom
    accessibility is more likely to influence employment outcomes.
-   We exclude individuals who did not start a job due to illness or
    disability; family responsibilities; or full-time studies or
    training.
-   We exclude individuals who are unemployed due to temporary lay-off.
-   We exclude individuals who are working outside Canada.

These restrictions is made to focus the analysis on respondents for whom
accessibility is more likely to influence employment outcomes.

```{r}
respondents_filtered <- respondents %>%
  filter(
    # Place of residence 5 years ago, code 6: Same address (dwelling)
    Mob5 == 6, 
    # Main reason for not working the full year
    # Removing cases in which the person could not work the full year due to school, 
    # illness or disability, family responsibilities, pregnancy, retirement, seasonal work, etc
    MRNFY2 %in% c(-5, # Worked full year in 2020 or did not work since January 1, 2020
    5, # Unable to find work that lasted the full year
    7, # Personal choice
    9, # Other
    11 # Business conditions
    ), 
    # Reasons unable to start a job
    # Removing cases in which the person could not start a job due to school, 
    # illness or disability, family responsibilities, etc
    REASN %in% c(-5, # Hours > 0 or LOOKWORK = No
                 1, # Could have started work, but did not find one
                 2, # Already had a job
                 6 # Other
                 ),
    # LayAB - Labour: On temporary lay-off or absent from job or business
   !LayAB %in% c(-2), # remove cases of temporary lay-off
   # Commuting: Place of work status
   !PWStat %in% c(5), # Removing cases of people with a work address outside Canada 
   !is.na(SA_pp_Active), 
   !is.na(SA_pp_Transit), 
   !is.na(SA_pp_Car), 
   !is.na(MMSA_pp_Active), 
   !is.na(MMSA_pp_Transit), 
   !is.na(MMSA_pp_Car))
```

# First stage

We will start the first stage of regression by creating a formula to
regress accessibility based on spatial filters and other variables.

```{r}
design_respondents <- svydesign(ids = ~1, 
                                data = respondents_filtered, 
                                weights = ~CompW1)
```

## Active IV

Creating the first stage for active accessibility (SA):

```{r}
stage1_Active_SA <- svyglm(SA_pp_Active ~
    # Accessibility - SA
    Sf_SA_pp_Active + SA_pp_Car + SA_pp_Transit + 
    
    # Socio-demography
    AGE + Gender + Disability + Temporary_or_refugee + Visible_minority +
    
    # Household info 
    Single_parent + CFKID0T5 + CFCNT_PP + 
    
    # Labour_force
    Weeks +
      
    # Neighbourhood and environmental
    Pop_centre + Pop_density,
    
    design = design_respondents)

summary(stage1_Active_SA, diagnostics = TRUE)
```

```{r}
regTermTest(stage1_Active_SA, ~ Sf_SA_pp_Active)
```

## Adding the instrumental variables 

Adding the instrumental variables to the data frame:

```{r}
respondents_filtered <- respondents_filtered %>%
  mutate(
    # SA 
    SA_pp_Active_IV = predict(stage1_Active_SA, newdata = ., type = "response"),
    SA_pp_Active_Res_IV = SA_pp_Active - SA_pp_Active_IV,  
    
    SA_pp_Transit_IV = predict(stage1_Transit_SA, newdata = ., type = "response"),
    SA_pp_Transit_Res_IV = SA_pp_Transit - SA_pp_Transit_IV,  
    
    SA_pp_Car_IV = predict(stage1_Car_SA, newdata = ., type = "response"),
    SA_pp_Car_Res_IV = SA_pp_Car - SA_pp_Car_IV,  
    
    # MMSA 
    MMSA_pp_Active_IV = predict(stage1_Active_MMSA, newdata = ., type = "response"),
    MMSA_pp_Active_Res_IV = MMSA_pp_Active - MMSA_pp_Active_IV,  
    
    MMSA_pp_Transit_IV = predict(stage1_Transit_MMSA, newdata = ., type = "response"),
    MMSA_pp_Transit_Res_IV = MMSA_pp_Transit - MMSA_pp_Transit_IV,  
    
    MMSA_pp_Car_IV = predict(stage1_Car_MMSA, newdata = ., type = "response"),
    MMSA_pp_Car_Res_IV = MMSA_pp_Car - MMSA_pp_Car_IV
    )
```

# Descriptive analysis

Before we perform the second stage, we will visualize some descriptive statistics about the variables used in the model. This function was created in order to produce an output in the format required by the RDC vetting process: 

```{r}
round_base5 <- function(x){
  return(round(x/5)*5)
  }

percent_round_mean <- function(raw_mean, nz_pop){
  p_table <- data.frame(lower = c(0, 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 320, 640, 1280),
                        upper = c(10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 320, 640, 1280, Inf),
                        p = c(16.67, 16.67, 10, 5, 2.5, 1.25, 0.625, 0.313, 0.156))
  
  p_val <- p_table$p[which(nz_pop >= p_table$lower & nz_pop < p_table$upper)]
  
  if(length(p_val) == 0){
    p_val <- 16.67
    } 
  
    max_abs_error<- (p_val/100) * abs(raw_mean)
  
  candidates <- c()
  k <- 0
  while(10^k <= max_abs_error * 10){
    candidates <- c(candidates, 10^k, 2*10^k, 5*10^k)
    k <- k+1
  }
  
  candidates <- sort(unique(candidates))
  
  candidates <- candidates[candidates <= max_abs_error]
  
  if(length(candidates) == 0){
    b <- 1e-6
  } else{
    b <- max(candidates)
  }
  
  rounded_mean <- round(raw_mean / b) * b
  return(rounded_mean)
}

create_descriptive_table_RDC <- function(df,vars,weight_col){
  if(!weight_col %in% names(df)){
    stop("Weight column not found")
  } 
  
  results <- list()
  
  for(var in vars){
    temp <- df[!is.na(df[[var]]), c(var, weight_col)]
    
    if(nrow(temp) == 0){
      next
    } 
  
    raw_w_n <- sum(temp[[weight_col]]) # raw weighted N
    raw_unw_n <- nrow(temp) # raw unweighted N
    rounded_w_n <- round_base5(raw_w_n) 
    rounded_unw_n <- round_base5(raw_unw_n)
    
  if(is.numeric(temp[[var]])){
      # calculate weighted mean
      w_mean <- weighted.mean(temp[[var]], temp[[weight_col]])
      
      # weighted sd 
      w_var <- sum(temp[[weight_col]]*(temp[[var]] - w_mean)^2)/(sum(temp[[weight_col]]) - 1)
      w_sd <- sqrt(w_var)
      
      # nonzero pop. size (raw, unrounded)
      nz_temp <- temp[temp[[var]] != 0,]
      nz_pop_raw <- sum(nz_temp[[weight_col]]) 
      
      # percent-round for the mean
      rounded_mean <- percent_round_mean(w_mean, nz_pop_raw)
      
      # standard deviation uses conventional rounding
      rounded_sd <- round(w_sd, 2)
      
      # rows
      ## for mean
      results[[paste0(var,"_mean")]] <- data.frame(
        Variable = var,
        Type = "Numeric",
        Subset = "Total population",
        Weighted_Pop = raw_w_n, 
        Weighted_Pop_Round5 = rounded_w_n,
        Unweighted_N = raw_unw_n,
        Nonzero_Pop = nz_pop_raw,
        Statistic = "Mean",
        Value = w_mean,
        Rounded_Value = rounded_mean,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
      
      ## for standard deviation
      results[[paste0(var,"_sd")]] <- data.frame(
        Variable = var,
        Type = "Numeric",
        Subset = "Total population",
        Weighted_Pop = raw_w_n, 
        Weighted_Pop_Round5 = rounded_w_n,
        Unweighted_N = raw_unw_n,
        Nonzero_Pop = nz_pop_raw,
        Statistic = "Std. Dev.",
        Value = w_sd,
        Rounded_Value = rounded_sd,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
      
    }else{
      # categorical cases
      cats <- unique(temp[[var]])
      for(cat in cats){
        cat_temp <- temp[temp[[var]] == cat,]
        
        #weighted count for this category
        raw_cat_w <- sum(cat_temp[[weight_col]])
        rounded_cat_w <- round_base5(raw_cat_w)
        
        #unweighted count for this category
        raw_cat_unw <- nrow(cat_temp)
        rounded_cat_unw <- round_base5(raw_cat_unw)
        
        # percentage = rounded count of the category/rounded total weighted 
        percentage <- (rounded_cat_w/rounded_w_n) * 100
        rounded_perc <- round(percentage, 2)
        
        results[[paste0(var,"_",cat)]] <- data.frame(
          Variable = var,
          Type = "Categoric",
          Subset = as.character(cat),
          Weighted_Pop = raw_w_n, 
          Weighted_Pop_Round5 = rounded_w_n,
          Unweighted_N = raw_unw_n,
          Nonzero_Pop = raw_w_n,
          Statistic = "Percentage",
          Value = percentage,
          Rounded_Value = rounded_perc,
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
      }
    }
  }
  
  final_table <- bind_rows(results)
  
  final_table$Rounded_Value <- round(final_table$Rounded_Value, 2)
  
  return(final_table)
}
```

```{r}
descriptive_analysis_general_pop <- create_descriptive_table_RDC(
  df = respondents_filtered,
  vars = c("SA_pp_Active", "SA_pp_Car", "SA_pp_Transit",
           "MMSA_pp_Active", "MMSA_pp_Car", "MMSA_pp_Transit", 
           "AGE", "Gender", "Disability", "Temporary_or_refugee", 
           "Visible_minority", "Single_parent", "CFKID0T5",
           "CFCNT_PP", "Weeks", "Pop_centre","Pop_density",
           "LBR_FORC_label", "LOKWK_label", "CfInc_AT"), 
  weight_col = "CompW1")

descriptive_analysis_general_pop
```

# Modelling demonstration

## Linear regression

First, we need to create a survey design object: 

```{r}
labour_force_design <- svydesign(ids = ~1, 
                                 data = respondents_filtered %>% 
                                 # Removing cases in which this 
                                 #  variable is not applicable (-3)
                                 filter(CfInc_AT > 0),   
                                 weights = ~CompW1)
```

Then, we can estimate the linear regression model: 

```{r}
labour_force_income_model <- survey::svyglm(
  # Outcome   
  CfInc_AT ~ 
    
  # We use the predicted accessibility indicators to control for endogeneity 
  # Accessibility - SA
  SA_pp_Active_IV + SA_pp_Car_IV + SA_pp_Transit_IV + 
    
  # Socio-demography
  AGE + Gender + Disability + Temporary_or_refugee + Visible_minority +
    
  # Household info 
  Single_parent + CFKID0T5 + CFCNT_PP + 
    
  # Labour_force
  Weeks +
      
  # Neighbourhood and environmental
  Pop_centre + Pop_density,
    
  design = labour_force_design,
  )

summary(labour_force_income_model)
```

Assessing the existence of multicollinearity (Tip: VIF \< 10):

```{r}
car::vif(labour_force_income_model)
```

Visualizing R2: 

```{r}
null_deviance <- labour_force_income_model$null.deviance
model_deviance <- labour_force_income_model$deviance
r_squared <- 1 - (model_deviance / null_deviance)
r_squared
```

## Logistic regression

Creating the formula:

```{r}
labour_force_employment_status_model <- survey::svyglm(
  # Outcome   
  LBR_FORC_label ~ 
    
  # Accessibility - SA
  SA_pp_Active + SA_pp_Car + SA_pp_Transit + 
    
  # Socio-demography
  AGE + Gender + Disability + Temporary_or_refugee + Visible_minority +
    
  # Household info 
  Single_parent + CFKID0T5 + CFCNT_PP + 
    
  # Labour_force
  Weeks +
      
  # Neighbourhood and environmental
  Pop_centre + Pop_density +
    
  # Use the residuals to control for endogeneity 
  SA_pp_Active_Res_IV + SA_pp_Car_Res_IV + SA_pp_Transit_Res_IV,
  design = labour_force_design,
  family = quasibinomial()
  )

summary(labour_force_employment_status_model)
```

Assessing the existence of multicollinearity (Tip: VIF \< 10):

```{r}
library(car)

vif_check <- lm(as.numeric(LBR_FORC_label) ~ 
    SA_pp_Active + SA_pp_Car + SA_pp_Transit +
    AGE + Gender + Disability + Temporary_or_refugee + Visible_minority +
    Single_parent + CFKID0T5 + CFCNT_PP + Weeks +
    Pop_centre + Pop_density +
    SA_pp_Active_Res_IV + SA_pp_Car_Res_IV + SA_pp_Transit_Res_IV,
  data = labour_force_design$variables)

car::vif(vif_check)
```

Creating a function to better visualize our model output:

```{r}
compute_or_table <- function(model){
  model_summary <- summary(model)
  coefs <- coef(model)
  se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(model)))
  
  # freedom degree for t-distribution
  df_resid <- degf(model$survey.design)
  
  # t-statistics and p-values
  t_stats <- coefs/se
  p_values <- 2*pt(-abs(t_stats), df = df_resid)  # Two-tailed
  
  # confidence intervals using t-distribution
  t_critical <- qt(1 - 0.05/2, df = df_resid)
  ci_lower <- coefs - t_critical * se
  ci_upper <- coefs + t_critical * se
  
  results <- data.frame(Variable = names(coefs),
    Coef = coefs,
    SE = se,
    t_value = t_stats,
    OR = exp(coefs),
    OR_lower = exp(ci_lower),
    OR_upper = exp(ci_upper),
    p_value = p_values,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  
  results$Change <- (results$OR-1)*100
  
  results$Effect <- with(results, {
    case_when(p_value >= 0.05 ~ "Insignificant",
      OR > 1.001 ~ "Positive",
      OR < 0.999 ~ "Negative",
      TRUE ~ "No Effect" # se OR ~= 1
    )
  })
  
  # To falicitate my interpretation of the results
  results$Sig <- with(results, {
    case_when(p_value < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p_value < 0.01 ~ "**",
      p_value < 0.05 ~ "*",
      p_value < 0.1 ~ ".",
      TRUE ~ "")
  })
  
  # round numeric columns
  num_cols <- c("Coef", "SE", "t_value", "OR", "OR_lower", 
                "OR_upper", "Change")
  results[num_cols] <- lapply(results[num_cols], round, 2)
  results$p_value <- signif(results$p_value, 3)  # p-values
  
  col_order <- c("Variable", "Coef", "SE", "t_value", 
                 "OR", "OR_lower", "OR_upper", "Change", "p_value", 
                 "Sig", "Effect")
  
  col_order <- col_order[col_order %in% names(results)]
  
  results <- results[,col_order]
  
  # interpretation column
  results$Interpretation <- with(results,{
    case_when(
      Effect == "Positive" ~ 
        sprintf("%s%% increase in odds (95%% CI: %s to %s)",
        round(Change, 1), round(OR_lower, 2), round(OR_upper, 2)),
      Effect == "Negative" ~ 
        sprintf("%s%% decrease in odds (95%% CI: %s to %s)",
        round(-Change, 1), round(OR_lower, 2), round(OR_upper, 2)),
      TRUE ~ "No significant effect")
  })
  
  return(results)
}

compute_elasticities <- function(model, 
                                 pct_increase=10){
  mf <- model.frame(model$survey.design)
  w <- weights(model$survey.design)
  
  pred_probs <- predict(model, type = "response")
  
  coefs <- coef(model)
  vcov_mat <- vcov(model)
  
  cont_vars <- intersect(names(coefs), colnames(mf))
  cont_vars <- cont_vars[cont_vars != "(Intercept)"]
  cont_vars <- cont_vars[sapply(mf[cont_vars], function(x) length(unique(na.omit(x))) > 2)]
  cont_vars <- cont_vars[cont_vars %in% names(coefs)]
  
  scale_factor <- pct_increase/1  
  
  elas <- sapply(cont_vars, function(v) {
    x_mean <- weighted.mean(mf[[v]], w, na.rm = TRUE)
    p_mean <- weighted.mean(pred_probs, w, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    elas_1pct <- coefs[v] * x_mean / p_mean
    elas_val <- elas_1pct * scale_factor
    elas_se <- sqrt((x_mean / p_mean)^2 * vcov_mat[v, v]) * scale_factor
    
    CI_lower <- elas_val - qnorm(1 - 0.05/2) * elas_se
    CI_upper <- elas_val + qnorm(1 - 0.05/2) * elas_se
    
    return(c(Elasticity = elas_val, `2.5%` = CI_lower, `97.5%` = CI_upper))
  })
  
  elas_df <- as.data.frame(t(elas))
  colnames(elas_df) <- c("Elasticity", "2.5%", "97.5%")
  elas_df$Variable <- rownames(elas_df)
  
  elas_df$Effect <- ifelse(elas_df$`2.5%` > 0, "Positive",
                           ifelse(elas_df$`97.5%` < 0, "Negative", "Insignificant"))
  
  elas_df <- elas_df[, c("Variable", "Elasticity", "2.5%", "97.5%", "Effect")]
  
  numeric_cols <- c("Elasticity", "2.5%", "97.5%")
  elas_df[numeric_cols] <- round(elas_df[numeric_cols], 3)
  rownames(elas_df) <- NULL
  
  return(elas_df)
}
```

## Multinomial regression

Creating a survey design object: 

```{r}
low_education_design <- svydesign(
  ids = ~1, 
  data = respondents_filtered %>% 
    # Filtering for education and selecting only unemployed people
    filter(Education == "High school or no certificate", 
           LOKWK_label %in% c("Yes (for full-time work)", 
                              "Yes (for part-time work)", 
                              "No")),   
 weights = ~CompW1)
```

Estimating the multinomial regression model: 

```{r}
low_education_jobseeking_model <- svy_vglm(
  # Outcome   
  LOKWK_label ~ 
    
  # Accessibility - SA
  SA_pp_Active + SA_pp_Car + SA_pp_Transit + 
    
  # Socio-demography
  AGE + Gender + Disability + Temporary_or_refugee + Visible_minority +
    
  # Household info 
  Single_parent + CFKID0T5 + CFCNT_PP + 
    
  # Labour_force
  Weeks +
      
  # Neighbourhood and environmental
  Pop_centre + Pop_density +
    
  # To control for endogeneity 
  SA_pp_Active_Res_IV + SA_pp_Car_Res_IV + SA_pp_Transit_Res_IV,
  design = low_education_design,
  family = multinomial()
  )

summary(low_education_jobseeking_model)
```
Assessing the existence of multicollinearity (Tip: VIF \< 10):

```{r}
vif_check <- lm(as.numeric(LOKWK_label) ~ 
    SA_pp_Active + SA_pp_Car + SA_pp_Transit +
    AGE + Gender + Disability + Temporary_or_refugee + Visible_minority +
    Single_parent + CFKID0T5 + CFCNT_PP + Weeks +
    Pop_centre + Pop_density +
    SA_pp_Active_Res_IV + SA_pp_Car_Res_IV + SA_pp_Transit_Res_IV,
  data = low_education_design$variables)

car::vif(vif_check)
```

```{r}
                     design = low_education_design,
```

Creating a function to better visualize our model output:

```{r}
make_multinom_OR_table <- function(model) {
    coef_mat <- coef(summary(model))
  
  est <- coef_mat[, "Estimate"]
  se  <- coef_mat[, "Std. Error"]
  p   <- coef_mat[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
  
  OR <- exp(est)
  CI_low  <- exp(est - 1.96 * se)
  CI_high <- exp(est + 1.96 * se)
  
  df <- tibble(raw_term = rownames(coef_mat),
    OR = OR,
    CI_low = CI_low,
    CI_high = CI_high,
    p_value = p)
  
  categories <- model@misc$ynames       
  ref_cat <- categories[1]             
  
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(Variable = str_replace(raw_term, ":(.*)$", ""),
      Cat = str_extract(raw_term, "(?<=:)\\d+"),
      Cat = as.integer(Cat),
      Comparison = paste0(categories[Cat + 1], " vs ", ref_cat)) %>%
    dplyr::select(Variable, Comparison, OR, p_value, CI_low, CI_high)
  
  df <- df %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(Interpretation = case_when(
        is.na(p_value) ~ "",
        p_value > 0.05 ~ "No significant effect",
        OR > 1 ~ "Increase in odds",
        OR < 1 ~ "Decrease in odds",
        TRUE ~ "No effect")) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  return(df)
}
```

Visualizing our model output with explanations:

```{r}
OR_table_low_education_jobseeking <- make_multinom_OR_table(low_education_jobseeking_model$fit)
OR_table_low_education_jobseeking
```

## Ordinal regression 

To perform an ordinal regression, first, is suggested to scale all numeric variables: 

```{r}
low_education_to_scale <- respondents_filtered %>% 
    # Filtering for education and selecting only unemployed people
    filter(Education == "High school or no certificate", 
           LOKWK_label %in% c("Yes (for full-time work)", 
                              "Yes (for part-time work)", 
                              "No")) %>% 
  # Creating an ordinal categorical variable based on after-tax income
   mutate(Income_quintile  = 
           cut(CfInc_AT,
               breaks = Hmisc::wtd.quantile(CfInc_AT, 
                                            weights = CompW1, 
                                            probs = c(0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1)),
               labels = c("1_quintile",
                          "2_quintile",
                          "3_quintile",
                          "4_quintile",
                          "5_quintile"),
               include.lowest = TRUE), 
         Income_quintile = factor(Income_quintile,
                                  levels = c("1_quintile",
                                             "2_quintile",
                                             "3_quintile",
                                             "4_quintile",
                                             "5_quintile"),
                                 ordered = TRUE))

vars_to_scale <- c(
  "MMSA_pp_Active", "MMSA_pp_Transit", "MMSA_pp_Car",
  "MMSA_pp_Active_Res_IV", "MMSA_pp_Transit_Res_IV", "MMSA_pp_Car_Res_IV", 
  "AGE", "CFKID0T5", "CFCNT_PP", "Weeks", "Pop_density"
  )

scaled_data <- low_education_to_scale %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(vars_to_scale), 
                function(x) {
                  scaled <- scale(x)
                  return(as.numeric(scaled))
                }))
```

Now, we create a design object:

```{r}
low_educated_design_scaled <- svydesign(
  ids = ~1,
  weights = ~CompW1,
  data = scaled_data)
```

Fitting the model:

```{r}
low_educated_income_quintile_model <- svyolr(
  # Outcome   
  Income_quintile ~ 
    
  # Accessibility - MMSA
  MMSA_pp_Active + MMSA_pp_Car + MMSA_pp_Transit + 
    
  # Socio-demography
  AGE + Gender + Disability + Temporary_or_refugee + Visible_minority +
    
  # Household info 
  Single_parent + CFKID0T5 + CFCNT_PP + 
    
  # Labour_force
  Weeks +
      
  # Neighbourhood and environmental
  Pop_centre + Pop_density +
    
  # To control for endogeneity 
  MMSA_pp_Active_Res_IV + MMSA_pp_Car_Res_IV + MMSA_pp_Transit_Res_IV,
  design = low_educated_design_scaled)

summary(low_educated_income_quintile_model)
```
# Confidentiality vetting

Confidentiality vetting is the process of reviewing the results to be
released by the Research Data Center to ensure that confidentiality
risks for StatCan respondents are minimized.

The following rules apply to our results:

-   *Statistics must not be released for identifiable areas with less
    than 40 persons (*$\sum{CompW1} ≥ 40$). Statistics must not be
    released for identifiable areas with less than 40 persons. This
    condition is usually met with geography levels used at the RDCs. The
    population threshold can be applied to the (long form) weighted
    population estimate.
-   *All statistics must be based on weighted data.*
-   *Statistics must be based on at least 5 respondents, whose sum of
    weights is at least 10*.
-   *Statistics (Means and total sums) are subject to a simplistic
    percent rounding by deterministically rounding to the nearest
    multiple of a rounding base.* The rounding base is set so that the
    rounded value is never more than p% away from the unrounded value.
    The value of p% is determined by the associated nonzero population
    size of the mean or total. It is the weighted number of records with
    a nonzero value. The table below outlines the maximum percentage
    difference (p%) from the unrounded value, based on its associated
    nonzero population size.

| Nonzero Pop. size | \<10 | 10-\<20 | 20-\<40 | 40-\<80 | 80-\<160 | 160-\<320 | 320-\<640 | 640-\<1280 | \>=1280 |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| p% | 16.67% | 16.67% | 10% | 5% | 2.5% | 1.25% | 0.625% | 0.313% | 0.156% |
